Womb Transplant - Journeyman Special

By: Wynand Grobler | Archived

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Womb transplant

Unique Selling Point:
Born without a uterus, Emelie Eriksson thought she was denied the opportunity to start the family she craved. However, all this changed thanks to the vision of Professor Mats Brännström and a donor womb from Emelie's mother. As she plays with her son, Emelie muses on the significance of this radical surgery. “This is something that you read in history books, and now in the future when you read about this, it’s about me.”

Script:


World's first womb transplant patient describes having her baby using her mother's uterus

Emelie Eriksson, of Bergshamra, Sweden, received a uterus transplant from her mother and later gave birth to her son Albin with the very same womb that bore her. “This is something that you read in history books and now in the future when you read about this, it’s about me.”
Eriksson was born without a womb and therefore unable to bear children. She was one of the first to undergo this revolutionary operation. The life work of doctor, Mats Brannstrom.


Names
Daniel Chrysong (father Albin) 1:02
Emelie Eriksson (mother Albin) 1:23
Mats Brännström, Gynecologist 3:03

Credits: Polygooi Productions
Report/Research :Cornelis van Groesen
Camera: Rob Vermaas

Scipt and narration

1: 00: 00: 05: 13 00: 00: 09: 16 04:03

When he wakes up in the morning,

he has a big smile on his face.



2: 00: 00: 11: 13 00: 00: 15: 02 03:14

He just takes on the world.



3: 00: 00: 15: 05 00: 00: 17: 22 02:17

He’s very charming, and gets a lot smiles



4: 00: 00: 18: 00 00: 00: 22: 22 04:22

When we go out to the stores



5: 00: 00: 23: 20 00: 00: 26: 12 02:17

Full of energy.



6: 00: 00: 26: 15 00: 00: 28: 17 02:02

A bundle of joy.



7: 00: 00: 28: 20 00: 00: 32: 09 03:14

Reporter: He’s your little miracle?

- Yes, he is my miracle. Well, our miracle actually.

0:35
VO: We are in the Swedish town of Bergshamra, an hour's drive from Stockholm. A lush green area covered in forests. An idyllic spot for a child. And Albin Eriksson is a very special child. He is the first child to be born from a transplanted womb.

8: 00: 00: 55: 00 00: 00: 58: 11 03:11

Hey. I'm Koen.

9: 00: 00: 58: 14 00: 01: 01: 15 03:01

My name is Koen.

- Albin.

10: 00: 01: 02: 15 00: 01: 06: 01 03:11

It's science fiction.

11: 00: 01: 06: 04 00: 01: 09: 21 03:17

I never thought it would be possible.




1:11
VO: Albin’s birth truly is a miracle. When his mother Emilie was 15 she received some earth-shattering news. She was born without a uterus, and was told she would never be able to give birth.

12: 00: 01: 23: 06 00: 01: 28: 08 05:02

It is devastating, because you always know...

That ev


13: 00: 01: 28: 11 00: 01: 33: 10 04:24

Even if you are very young

and playing with dolls ...



14: 00: 01: 33: 13 00: 01: 38: 07 04:19

... you always have this dream

That you will have a family.



15: 00: 01: 38: 10 00: 01: 43: 00 04:15

A big house, a car, a dog,

and then your own children.


16: 00: 01: 43: 03 00: 01: 45: 04 02:01

That is the dream you have.



17: 00: 01: 45: 07 00: 01: 49: 19 04:12

And then when someone takes away that dream ...



18: 00: 01: 49: 22 00: 01: 53: 20 03:23

... then something is missing.

You have a void in you.



19: 00: 01: 56: 16 00: 02: 02: 05 05:14

And then I met Daniel, that’s when ...



20: 00: 02: 02: 08 00: 02: 06: 14 04:06

... I began to think in those terms:



21: 00: 02: 06: 17 00: 02: 12: 20 06:03

What are we supposed to do

if we want to have a family?

22: 00: 02: 12: 23 00: 02: 14: 17 01:19

What are we going to do?

23: 00: 02 : 16: 23 00: 02: 28: 15

VO: Some friends told them about a radical new operation. At the univeristy hospital in Gothenburg, a surgeon called Mats Brannstrom wanted to perform the world’s first womb transplant.

24: 00: 02: 29: 20 00: 02: 32: 24 03:04

I did not really think very much about it.


24: 00: 02: 33: 02 00: 02: 37: 16 04:14

I was more like ‘yeah! let's do this

This is just awesome.’



25: 00: 02: 37: 19 00: 02: 43: 10 05:16

Daniel was the one who was thinking
what if.


26: 00: 02: 43: 13 00: 02: 48: 20 05:07

You have more chance of winning the lottery

then to do this.


27: 00: 02: 48: 23 00: 02: 53: 15 04:17

And I said, We'll see later.

2:54
VO: We meet up with this “miracle” doctor, as he prepares for surgery. He was exposed to this revolutionary idea by a patient, when he was working in Australia.

28: 00: 03: 03: 19 00: 03: 07: 04 03:10

I had to operate on a young patient,
Her name was Angela.


29: 00: 03: 07: 07 00: 03: 10: 17 03:10

She had cervical cancer.

She was 25.


30: 00: 03: 10: 20 00: 03: 14: 09 03:14

I had to remove her uterus with a radical hystorectomy.


31: 00: 03: 14: 12 00: 03: 17: 09 02:22

I told her you have your ovaries preserved ...



32: 00: 03: 17: 12 00: 03: 21: 21 04:09

... but you can not carry child

As you will not have a womb.



33: 00: 03: 21: 24 00: 03: 26: 00 04:01

And she said: Is this a problem. Can’t you

do a uterus transplantation?


34: 00: 03: 26: 03 00: 03: 29: 18 03:15

And she actually told me my mother or my

Sister could donate


35: 00: 03: 29: 21 00: 03: 32: 15 02:19

I was astonished, I had never thought about this.



36: 00: 03: 32: 18 00: 03: 36: 18 04:00

And we said well, we should start a research project on this.


37: 00: 03: 36: 21 00: 03: 41: 21 05:00

First, see if it worked in rodents,

starting with mice.



38: 00: 03: 41: 24 00: 03: 47: 17 05:18

After two, three years, we had

good results with the mice.



39: 00: 03: 47: 20 00: 03: 51: 02 03:07

Reporter: You came closer and closer to humans?



40: 00: 03: 51: 05 00: 03: 54: 17 03:12

I had estimated it would take about five years ...



41: 00: 03: 54: 20 00: 03: 59: 02 04:07

... but in the end it

lasted 14, 15 years.

4:00
VO: Doctor Brannstrom is ready for the first attempt on a human. The candidates must be suitable, but also have a willing donor within the family. Transplants from family members have a lower chance of rejection.


42: 00: 04: 11: 19 00: 04: 15: 05 03:11

I told my mom about the project.


43: 00: 04: 15: 08 00: 04: 17: 24 02:16

And she said to me:

44: 00: 04: 18: 02 00: 04: 23: 06 05:04

"If I give you my womb,

would it work? "



45: 00: 04: 23: 09 00: 04: 27: 22 04:13

And I said: Yes, that's the plan.




46: 00: 04: 28: 00 00: 04: 34: 17 06:17

My mother in law is terrified

for anesthesia.



47: 00: 04: 36: 04 00: 04: 40: 08 04:04

Afraid she will never wake up.

48: 00: 04: 41: 12 00: 04: 45: 14 04:02

It was no ordinary operation.

You did not know how it would go ...



49: 00: 04: 45: 17 00: 04: 48: 16 02:24

... with my mother or me.

4:50
VO: The operation is so complex that they begin at the crack of dawn.



50: 00: 04: 55: 18 00: 05: 02: 01 06:08

Of course we try to sleep well,

because it is a time consuming operation.


51: 00: 05: 02: 04 00: 05: 06: 06 04:02

It is a long day starting
from 7 am to 10 pm.



52: 00: 05: 06: 09 00: 05: 08: 20 02:11

With a large surgical team ...



53: 00: 05: 08: 23 00: 05: 13: 02 04:04

... about ten doctors

and a lot of nurses.


54: 00: 05: 13: 05 00: 05: 16: 18 03:13

The same team, that for years

had practiced with animals.



55: 00: 05: 16: 21 00: 05: 20: 06 03:10

So trained exactly at
what we are best at.


56: 00: 05: 21: 04 00: 05: 25: 06 04:02

The night before the operation.

I did not sleep.



57: 00: 05: 25: 09 00: 05: 29: 03 03:19

I got at the hospital, nervous.



58: 00: 05: 29: 06 00: 05: 34: 00 04:19

Freshly showered

with that hospital soap.



5:38
VO: First, the womb is removed from Emelie’s mother. The operation is technically challenging.

59: 00: 05: 46: 01 00: 05: 49: 04 03:03

The problem is we have to get
very long blood vessels


60: 00: 05: 49: 07 00: 05: 52: 15 03:08

And the problem with the uterus is that it ...


61: 00: 05: 52: 18 00: 05: 56: 19 04:01

... is located down in the pelvis, in a sort of funnel.


62: 00: 05: 56: 22 00: 06: 00: 08 03:11

So we have very little exposure

to get to the vessels.

6:02
VO: Therefore the uterus is removed with the blood vessels attached and placed on ice. The blood vessels are continuously rinsed with preservative. Then the uterus is transplated into the recipient.

63: 00: 06: 15: 04 00: 06: 20: 05 05:01

And then we release the clamps

and it is connected

on the circulatory system of the recipient.



64: 00: 06: 21: 02 00: 06: 23: 07 02:05

Then it is alive again.



65: 00: 06: 23: 10 00: 06: 26: 20 03:10

We realized we had done something big.



66: 00: 06: 26: 23 00: 06: 29: 22 02:24

Of course I was hoping for this ...



67: 00: 06: 30: 00 00: 06: 34: 11 04:11

... but I was only assured

when it was successful.

6:34
VO: The operation was a resounding success. This was the first ever womb transplant. But there is always the chance of rejection. And this seems to be the case with Emelie.

68: 00: 06: 47: 14 00: 06: 52: 20 05:06

But then when you body rejects it…
It is like: NO!



69: 00: 06: 52: 23 00: 06: 56: 13 03:15

No, not now we have come so far.


70: 00: 06: 56: 16 00: 07: 01: 11 04:20

And no one could really tell me

whether it would be all right again..

7:02
VO: Eventually, they found medication to manage the rejection. And one year after the surgery, a fertilized embryo was placed in Emilie’s uterus.


71: 00: 07: 11: 18 00: 07: 16: 18 05:00

The doctor gave me a pregnancy test

I had take it after a few weeks.



72: 00: 07: 16: 21 00: 07: 20: 10 03:14

I did, but when it was negative.



73: 00: 07: 20: 13 00: 07: 23: 08 02:20

That was terrible.



74: 00: 07: 23: 11 00: 07: 27: 07 03:21

Then after a week she still didn’t get her period.



75: 00: 07: 27: 10 00: 07: 30: 15 03:05

I said, do another test.



76: 00: 07: 30: 18 00: 07: 33: 19 03:01

And then I could see that I was pregnant.
Yeah…


77: 00: 07: 44: 10 00: 07: 50: 00 05:15

When Albin was born, he began

screaming. And I realized:



78: 00: 07: 50: 03 00: 07: 53: 08 03:05

This is quite real.



79: 00: 07: 53: 11 00: 07: 58: 13 05:02

I have a child, we are a family.

This is our own son.



80: 00: 07: 58: 16 00: 08: 01: 20 03:04

I fainted.



81: 00: 08: 01: 23 00: 08: 05: 01 03:03

All the emotions?

- It was just too much.

8:06
VO: Albin was born by caesarean section, performed by Dr Brannstrom himself. His dream, which he had been researching for 15 years, had become a reality.

82: 00: 08: 17: 01 00: 08: 23: 11 06:10

I have five children myself

and I know how great it is.



83: 00: 08: 23: 14 00: 08: 27: 14 04:00

My greatest reward

is to see the families together.



84: 00: 08: 27: 17 00: 08: 32: 18 05:01

Emelie and her husband send me

photos and videos of Albin.



85: 00: 08: 32: 21 00: 08: 36: 13 03:17

Then I see how happy

I made them.



86: 00: 08: 37: 13 00: 08: 40: 23 03:10

What will we write?

- Mom.

Mamma. Pappa. Albin.

87: 00: 08: 51: 10 00: 08: 56: 05 04:20

Albin is maybe part of a new

future, also for Dutch women.



88: 00: 08: 56: 08 00: 09: 00: 22 04:14

I sincerely hope

that an operation like this ...



89: 00: 09: 01: 00 00: 09: 06: 07 05:07

... gives an opportunity for everyone,

anywhere in the world.



90: 00: 09: 09: 13 00: 09: 13: 06 03:18

Because it is just super for everyone.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Born without a uterus, Emelie Eriksson thought she was denied the opportunity to start the family she craved. However, all this changed thanks to the vision of Professor Mats Brännström and a donor womb from Emelie's mother. As she plays with her son, Emelie muses on the significance of this radical surgery. “This is something that you read in history books, and now in the future when you read about this, it’s about me.”
